newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota says undecided on India car output.
newsitem.headline: Toyota says undecided on India car output.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp said on Wednesday it had not decided on whether to make cars in India.
The Nihon Keizai Shimbun economic daily said on Wednesday that Toyota and Daihatsu would set up a joint venture in India with the Kirloskar group in the middle of 1997 for car production in 1999.

"Toyota and Daihatsu started a feasibility study (for car production in India) with the Kirloskar group in October. We are currently conducting the study but we have not yet decided on anything specific, including what models and how many cars we would produce," a Toyota spokeswoman said.
Daihatsu Motor Co Ltd, which specialises in small cars and commerical vehicles, is 33.4 percent owned by Toyota.
Total investment will be 30 billion to 50 billion yen, the newspaper said.
The venture will produce passenger cars and recreational vehicles and aim for output of 100,000 units annually, the paper said.
